goal: Gather, organize and synthesize information on the issue: advanced searches on a shared classroom device (printed clippings on the paper path), an interview, a short survey of peers run through the school, or an information request to the named office sent through an adult; an organized source record and a synthesis that begins the factual report.
note: Surveys carry no personal questions and go through the school. An information request sent today has about two and a half weeks to bring a reply before the day 80 look back. On the paper path NML.T5.1's digital tools are met in part, said plainly to the teacher, as for NML.T5.4 and T5.5 in unit 9. The source record and synthesis are scored with the unit assessment for T5.1.

goal: Finish the factual report and write an editorial on the issue (about a page each), with one student-made visual captioned for each piece (a digital graphic on a shared device, or a drawn one on the paper path); explain how the two kinds of writing differ, then revise.
note: Lean ela:W.11-12.2 and W.11-12.1: argument taught in ELA 12 unit 2 (by about day 38) and in grade 10; informative writing in ELA 11 unit 2. On the paper path NML.T5.3's digital tools are met in part, said plainly to the teacher. Both pieces and the visual are scored with the unit assessment for T5.2 and T5.3. Also met: RH.11-12.7, WHST.11-12.1, WHST.11-12.2.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: an unseen past policy and its record: judge its intended and unintended results and how parties, groups and media shaped it.
codes: MA.GOV.T4.6; MA.GOV.T4.6a; MA.GOV.T4.6b; MA.GOV.T4.6c; MA.GOV.T4.6d; MA.GOV.T4.6e; D2.Civ.13.9-12; MA.GOV.T4.7; MA.NML.T4.4; MA.NML.T5.1; MA.NML.T5.2; MA.NML.T5.3
note: Parts asked, a short prompt for each part the main task misses: a past and a current debate compared, with how parties, groups and media shaped opinion (T4.6, its lettered parts as options; day 65's comparison scored); the policy judged by intended and unintended results (D2.Civ.13); a current issue and who influences lawmaking on it (T4.7); a report, a post and an opinion piece taken apart (NML.T4.4, unseen items). Scored on the course rubric from the unit's products, not retaken: the day 68 source record and synthesis (NML.T5.1), the day 69 report, editorial and their difference (NML.T5.2) and the visuals (NML.T5.3).

goal: Respond to the end-of-unit assessment: reteach the weakest items in small groups and extend the rest.
note: The response time for the end-of-unit assessment, counted once here.

goal: Course-level check 2, final (units 1 to 8, weighted to 5 to 8): an unseen news package on a policy issue: source it, separate report from opinion, and explain how rights, branches and groups bear on it.
note: School day 72, week 15. It falls right after unit 8's assessment (day 70), so its items on unit 8's skills draw content from earlier units: the news package's issue is a rights, federalism or election question from units 3 to 6, never a unit 8 debate or a team's issue.

goal: Respond to course-level check 2: reteach the weakest items, then confirm each team's readiness for unit 9 (issue, outside expert if the teacher has arranged one, plan) and revise the plan.
note: Outside contact, where there is one, is arranged by the teacher through school staff or a teaching parent before unit 9 opens. Last ten minutes: unit 9's readiness check on ss8-civic-action and wh2-global-problems (last used grade 10).

goal: In teams: weigh the competing views on the local issue, judge how well the people and bodies involved have handled it, seek a compromise, and find real ways to take part, including how to contact local officials and comment at a public meeting.
note: Check set kept inside T4.8: contacting officials and public meetings in the student's own place, no added day. Structured deliberation (unit 9). Community voice: Sensitivity agent read with the unit plan (docs/pipeline/briefs/sensitivity-read.md): the community the issue concerns, from its own published voice. Partial base: American Government 3e (retired CC BY), chapters 1 and 14.

goal: Draft position papers and plan the team's portfolio: a digital portfolio, multipage site or podcast on a shared classroom device and an adult's account, or a printed portfolio on the paper path.
note: Both routes in the same days: the digital route uses a shared device and an adult's account; the paper route is a printed portfolio and is complete on its own (NML.T5.4 then met in part, said plainly to the teacher). Unit 8's report, editorial and visuals may supply content.

goal: Build the portfolio and work with contributors: where the teacher has arranged an outside expert through school staff or a teaching parent, the team exchanges drafts with them online through an adult's account on the classroom device; otherwise the team writes to a named office by letter through an adult and works with classmates as contributors.
note: The outside expert is optional (frame, For the lead 1). An online exchange with the expert meets NML.T5.5 in full; without one, NML.T5.5 is met in part, said plainly to the teacher. A recorded talk alone is a source, not collaboration. No student account, no public posting.

goal: Take the chosen action through a safe route (a public comment at the meeting found on day 66 where it falls in weeks 15 and 16, or in writing where the body accepts written comment; a letter sent through an adult; a proposal presented), or the declining route: an evidence-based information request sent through an adult or a nonpartisan information piece given to a consenting audience.
note: The year's informed action; the student's choice informed by evidence, never a cause the course picks. No student discloses immigration status or family details. Practised: D4.6.9-12, D4.7.9-12.

goal: Present the portfolio and position to the class or a consenting audience, and answer questions on the evidence.
note: Lean ela:SL.11-12.1: seminar norms known from earlier grades.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: an unseen local policy case from short sources: judge the bodies involved, weigh the views and propose a compromise; the team portfolio is scored on the same rubric.
note: Parts asked, a short prompt for each part the main task misses: working with classmates on a local issue, competing views, a compromise, ways to take part and position papers (T4.8, day 75's papers scored); citizens' and institutions' effectiveness judged (D2.Civ.5); civic virtues and democratic principles in teamwork (D2.Civ.7, the day 74 to 78 look-for record of each student's own contribution); a decision made and an action taken (D4.8, the day 77 action record). The team portfolio is scored on the same rubric for NML.T5.4 (in part on the paper route) and the collaboration record for NML.T5.5 (in part without an online exchange). School days 79 and 80 fall in week 16, the half's finals week.

goal: Respond to the end-of-unit assessment, then the look back at the day 68 request and the day 77 action: what changed, the response or its absence, and what the student would do next.
note: The response time for the end-of-unit assessment, counted once here.
